title: Implement hold preservation loop bypassing tone chain
description:
Add the dedicated Hold preservation path to Source/DSP/DelayVoice.h and Source/DSP/DelayVoice.cpp. DelayVoice is owned only by this task in this phase.

Before editing, inspect:
- Source/DSP/DelayVoice.h and .cpp (the existing repeat loop and its stage order)
- Source/DSP/SafetyProcessor.h as produced by f.3 (ceiling application, NaN/Inf rejection, DC blocker; read only)
- Source/DSP/FeedbackController.h as produced by f.2 (read only)

Required behavior, restated so no external document is needed:
- The normal repeat-loop order inside each voice's feedback loop is exactly: fractional delay read, HPF, LPF, Presence Guard, repeat transient softener, mild saturation, restricted diffusion, feedback tap. Do not reorder it.
- On Hold engage: new delay input goes to zero, and the loop crossfades over 30 ms equal-power into a dedicated Hold path.
- The Hold path bypasses HPF, LPF, Presence Guard, transient softening, saturation, and diffusion. This is a product behavior (freeze without progressive dulling), not an optimization, and must not be simplified into "reuse the normal loop with neutral settings".
- The Hold path retains: fractional delay read, routing, stereo channel exchange, DC blocker, NaN and infinity rejection, the hard 0.985 ceiling, and emergency safety handling.
- g_hold = 0.985, giving a long-decaying freeze whose tail does not progressively darken.
- Hold release is click-free and uses the same 30 ms equal-power crossfade back to the normal loop.
- Delay read positions remain clamped to [8 samples, 8.25 seconds] in both the normal and Hold paths.

Real-time rules that are binding: all maximum-size buffers are allocated in prepareToPlay/prepare; the per-block and per-sample paths perform no heap allocation, locks, IO, string construction, GUI calls, buffer resizing, or unbounded loops, and destroy no heap-owned objects.

Provide at minimum: DelayVoice::setHold(bool) and internal hold crossfade state. Do not add parameters or APVTS wiring here.
acceptance_criteria: Source/DSP/DelayVoice.h declares a Hold engage/release setter and internal hold crossfade state
Source/DSP/DelayVoice.cpp implements a dedicated Hold path that does not call the HPF, LPF, Presence Guard, transient softener, saturation, or diffusion stages
Source/DSP/DelayVoice.cpp retains fractional delay read, DC blocking, NaN and infinity rejection, and the 0.985 ceiling inside the Hold path
Source/DSP/DelayVoice.cpp zeroes new delay input while Hold is engaged and uses g_hold = 0.985
Source/DSP/DelayVoice.cpp implements a 30 ms equal-power crossfade for both Hold engage and Hold release
The normal repeat-loop stage order fractional delay read, HPF, LPF, Presence Guard, transient softener, saturation, diffusion, feedback tap is unchanged
Delay read positions are clamped to a minimum of 8 samples and a maximum of 8.25 seconds in both the normal and Hold paths
The DelayVoice audio path contains no new/delete, malloc, buffer resize, juce::String construction, or lock acquisition
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified
forbidden_changes: modify Source/DSP/RoutingEngine.h, Source/DSP/RoutingEngine.cpp, Source/DSP/SafetyProcessor.h, Source/DSP/SafetyProcessor.cpp, Source/DSP/FeedbackController.h, or Source/DSP/FeedbackController.cpp
implement Hold by reusing the normal tone chain with neutral coefficients
reorder or remove stages of the normal repeat loop
raise g_hold above 0.985 or bypass the ceiling during Hold
allocate memory or resize buffers in the audio path

allowed: choose internal member names for hold crossfade state
choose whether the hold path is a separate private member function or an inlined branch, provided the tone stages are genuinely skipped
forbidden: introduce a new voice or loop abstraction
change the DelayVoice public process signature
add APVTS parameters or host-facing wiring
collapse the Hold path into the normal tone chain
